### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via resolveUserAuthzGrants (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class), /api/v1/security/my-delegable-scope (route, the route ledger binds it to client method security.describeDelegableScope))_
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via explainAccessForCaller (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via resolveUserAuthzGrants (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via resolveUserAuthzGrants (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ResolvedAuthzContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via buildContextForUser (symbol, a top-level function), resolveUserAuthzGrants (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f968d1acecd9894b62fd6b69471b3ef6dee46f18` — the merge of head `0239ff1635ef4879e49ebaea37190839f4f402f6` into base `6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f968d1acecd9894b62fd6b69471b3ef6dee46f18 && git checkout f968d1acecd9894b62fd6b69471b3ef6dee46f18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1 0239ff1635ef4879e49ebaea37190839f4f402f6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1 && git merge --no-ff 0239ff1635ef4879e49ebaea37190839f4f402f6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6862ef62abd9062b54e92a8d8f82ec1abf1320c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Check-runs on the head: 47 check-runs, 39 success, 8 skipped (opt-in harnesses and matrix placeholders: `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Docs`, `Lint UI`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the `Test UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` shard placeholders), 0 failed, 0 in progress. `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check`, red on the previous head `32fe4f1b`, are green here, as are all eight `Test Core` shards, `Type Check UI`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

Reviewed against card #24757 (body and all 18 comments, rulings `6290781571`, 「甲」 as amended, unlock `6392096931`, claims `6414302166`, dev reports `6414056485` and the addendum `6417094296`) and card #25799 (body and all 5 comments, seat ruling A and S1 in claims `6414107849` / `6414315157`), the PR body (declarations unchanged between the two heads), its 39-file list, the net diff of `df4eb65c` against merge base `1bbb7bf4` (+1005 / −2552 over 39 files; −1907 of it the two deleted scripts), and the two-commit repair diff `32fe4f1b..df4eb65c` (5 files, +20 / −13) that followed the first round of this review.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Resolver request narrows to the context's set names** (`security-plugin-permission-sets.ts`: `const requested = [...explicitPermissionSets]`, baseline pushed after; `security-plugin.ts` drops the `dropDeactivatedFoldedSets` method and its `GUEST_POSITION` import). A held position's NAME no longer resolves a same-named set. **Right.** This is #13419 ruling B as ordered on #24757 (`6290781571`: HotCRM declares first, released in hotcrm `v6.0.0` per the unlock `6392096931`), shipped in 18.x under 「甲」 as amended. The guest arm (`positions = isGuest ? [] : …`) is kept, so ADR-0138 D3 item 3 holds for the guest by construction rather than by exclusion. The deleted second activation read is correct to delete: every name the plugin now requests arrived already judged by core's `readDisabledCatalogNames` (§6a/§6b), and `permission-set-active.test.ts` pins that a held position issues no ledger read. The four deleted pins on the ledger's 0/1 storage shape and type-scoped rows pinned that second reader, which no longer exists; core's own resolver tests parameterise `active` and `metadata_type` for the one reader left.

2. **The loud half** (`reportUngrantedNamesakeSets`, event `position_name_fold_grant`, payload `event`/`position`/`permissionSet` unchanged, `removedIn: 'next_major'` replaced by `granted: false`, new text with no tracker id). **Right.** 要点 5 is honoured: the difference is a warning, never a silent change. The probe resolves the held position names the request did not already name through the same evaluator and the same three sources, and what comes back is never granted (`namesakes` is only iterated, never merged into `permissionSets`). The predicate reads `requested` after the baseline push, so a baseline-named position stays silent, and once-per-name dedupe keys on a name that actually had a namesake. Read in the cited evaluator: an empty candidate list returns `[]` before any source is read; a catalog-loader failure is swallowed and warned once as a lookup failure, so the probe cannot fail the authorization resolution. `removedIn` was a log-payload key that shipped on 2026-10-20 (`f90ea677c`) and nothing in the tree consumes it; dropping it is a log change, not a published surface. Observation, not a finding: a held position with no namesake (`everyone`, `org_member`) is re-probed on every unmemoized resolution, which is a second `metadata.list('permission')` call per such resolution. The fold made equivalent catalog reads for the same names in the one evaluator call; the docblock states the cadence.

3. **`describePositionGrants` serves `via: 'definition'` only** (`security-plugin.ts`: `resolvePermissionSets(declared, …)`, `via: 'definition'` unconditionally). **Right**, and the test pins that no summary carries any other `via`. `PositionGrantVia` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts:130` still publishes `'definition' | 'name'`; the `'name'` member is published and unemitted until #26022 (open, `Blocked-by: #24757`) retires it. Nothing reads `'name'` to grant anything (the objectui badge renders it; HotCRM and objectui construct neither core type and read no `'name'` member at their pins), so the transitional state is sound.

4. **Delegated-admin gate** (`delegated-admin-gate.ts`: `setsCarriedByPosition` returns `[...new Set(listed)]`; `ownNameNote` deleted). **Right.** A set that only shares the position's name is granted by nothing after item 1, so judging it would refuse assignments that hand out nothing. Both consumers (the organization-level boundary and the delegated walk through `setsBoundToPosition`) read the one function, and the gate and the resolver read the same security catalog, so there is no window in which the gate admits what the resolver grants. This is a widening of what a delegate may assign relative to `main`, and it is the correct one; the unit and the three-posture suites each keep a teeth control (a LISTED set outside the allowlist is still refused, a LISTED admin set still cannot be self-delegated).

5. **Explain attribution** (`explain-engine.ts`: `positionBindingsOf` reads each held position's definition from the security catalog; `viaOf` says `position:P` when P's definition names the set, `direct grant + position:P` when `context.directPermissions` also names it, `position:P (whether a direct grant also names it could not be read)` under `directPermissionsUnread`, `direct grant` otherwise, and `direct grant or position definition (the position definitions could not be read)` when the catalog is unreadable). **Right.** Ruling A is honoured: the dual case names both channels. `via` is `z.string().optional()` in `explain.zod.ts`, so the wording moves no published accept set, and the dev's claim to that effect holds. Two bounded readings: a set named by two held definitions is attributed to the first in held order (the one channel a position grants through; sufficient for the card's distinction), and a context the resolver did not build and that carries no split (an agent acting for a user, a hand-built context without `principalKind`) reads `position:P` alone, which is today's reading and what S1 asks for.

6. **Core: `directPermissions: string[]` on `UserAuthzGrants` and `ResolvedAuthzContext`** (`resolve-authz-context.ts`: pushed in the §6 loop over `applyingGrants`, after the tenant/anchor filter and only when `active`, never from the §6a `boundSetNames` loop; initialised `[]` in all three literals; copied into `ctx` beside `permissions`). **Right**, and it is the split the resolver already computed: `applyingGrants` is the row set §6 confers from, so the field cannot disagree with `permissions` about which direct rows applied. Both types are exported from `@objectstack/core` (`security/index.ts:223,225`). The field is REQUIRED, not optional: additive for every reader, a compile-time change for code that builds either object as a literal. That is what the previous head's `Type Check · workspace` red measured: `packages/plugins/plugin-audit` test literals built envelopes without it, and the repair adds `directPermissions: []` to the three literals (`comment-access-hooks.test.ts` twice, `agent-dual-attribution.integration.test.ts` once), changing no assertion. Out of the repo, objectstack-ai/hotcrm and objectui at their checkouts build neither type. Required is the right choice (an optional field would let a hand-built context silently read as "no direct grants"), and the changeset states the one-line fix. See ②.

7. **Self path** (`security-plugin-explain-access.ts`: `else if (principalKind === 'human' && isSystem !== true && !onBehalfOf?.userId && userId)` re-resolves through `resolveUserAuthzGrants(this.ql, userId, { tenantId, nowMs, bypassGrantsCache: true })` and attaches only `directPermissions`, else `directPermissionsUnread: true`; the context's grants stay the request's). **Right.** Ruling S1 is honoured: agent, guest, service and system callers take neither branch and keep the context as it arrived; the dev's C2 ablation (re-resolve for every non-system caller) reds the agent pin. The premise holds in the cited spec: `ExecutionContextSchema` is a strip-mode `z.object`, so a transport parse drops an unknown `directPermissions` key, and the split cannot ride the envelope without a spec change. Cost: one extra resolver run per human self-explanation on a diagnostic endpoint, and the spread context is a new object so the per-context set memo misses once; both acceptable for explain. `directPermissionsUnread` is a private context key read only by `viaOf`.

8. **Goldens and ledgers.** Each exclusion or extension was judged on whether it hides a behaviour change:
   - `resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json` and its test docblock: the field is ADDED to every fixture and compared (not excluded). The values are consistent with the fixtures' own grant rows (the `u_ta` fixture lists `low` and not the position-bound `organization_admin`; the admin fixture lists both its direct rows). Legitimate; the pin is extended.
   - `request-rounds.test.ts` and `explain-engine.test.ts` (`buildContextForUser`): exact envelopes extended with the field. Legitimate.
   - `platform-admin-config.test.ts` posture-invariance arm: compares `single` against `isolated` WITHOUT the field. Legitimate, and the one place the new field truly differs between arms: under `single` the legacy organization-less `admin_full_access` row anchors and is in `applyingGrants` (so it is direct); walled, the row applies nowhere and the 6b-config anchor confers the set, which §6 does not push. The standing (`permissions`, `systemPermissions`, positions) is identical across arms, which is what the test pins; the channel is not the standing. Not a hidden change.
   - `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`, `grant-permission-set-name.equivalence.test.ts`, `resolve-authz-grant-set-by-name.golden.test.ts`: strip the field before comparing to goldens recorded before it existed. Legitimate: these pin the grant envelope, and the stripped field grants nothing. Note, not a finding: extending those goldens would have pinned the split on a real engine; the split is pinned on the recording double in core's new `direct-permissions.test.ts` and on a real resolver run in `explain-position-set-attribution.test.ts` and `explain-self-direct-grant.test.ts`.
   - `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: records the new self-explain double's `findOne` (which asserts the engine's predicate). A ledger entry the gate itself writes; legitimate.

9. **Gate retirement and gate-roster repairs.** `.github/workflows/lint.yml` loses the one step (both invocations); at the head no other line of the workflow names the step or its id. `scripts/check-position-name-fold-loaders.mjs` and `scripts/measure-position-name-fold-census.mjs` deleted; `dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` loses the gate's walked-roots block; `dispatch-gates.mjs` docblock repointed to the two remaining `#selfTest` anchors; `dispatch-gates.data.mjs` holds no entry (verified at the head). **Right**: the gate pinned that the fold's only in-repo route was test-only, and the route is gone. Remaining mentions (`scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs`, `scripts/measure-reserved-identity-name-census.mjs`, `scripts/check-workflow-step-name-quoting.mjs` fixture strings, `docs/audits/*`) are comments, fixtures and history.

10. **Test fixtures moved from name-granting to declared or direct grants.** First round: `security-plugin.test.ts` D10 harness now seeds `sys_user_permission_set` and a fake `registry` so direct grants resolve through the catalog; `controlled-by-parent-chain-middle-master.test.ts`; `permission-set-resolution-memo.test.ts`; `guest-grants-channel.test.ts` and `orgless-position-name-fold.test.ts` keep a control that the same set resolves when named. Repair round: `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.test.ts` (`pwr_manager`, `pwr_rep`) and `packages/cli/test/verify-parent-write-reach.test.ts` (`vpw_manager`) declared positions with a same-named permission set and no `permissionSets`, so their holders were reaching the set through the fold alone; each position now names its set (`permissionSets: ['pwr_manager']` etc.). **Right, and a pin move rather than a weakening**: the repair diff touches only the fixture declarations, no `expect` or assertion line moves in either file, so every verdict those suites pin (the parent-write reach of a manager against a rep, the control hook's refusal) is now reached through the declared binding ADR-0131 D3/D4 names, which is exactly the migration the changeset prescribes. These are also the two suites that would have fallen in the then-in-progress `Test Core` shards on the previous head; on this head all eight shards are green.

11. **Prose-only corrections in `resolve-authz-context.ts`** (repair round: the `readDisabledCatalogNames` docblock no longer lists the fold as a second reader; `readPositionGrantsInForce` says the definition is the whole answer; the guest-anchor docblock and the §6a "dropped from `positions`" comment no longer explain the drop by a fold that requests no set any more). **Right**: no code line moves in that commit's hunks of this file; the §6a drop itself is kept, for the reason the comment now states (no downstream reader sees a switched-off position as held). This closes the stale-prose flag the first round carried for this file.

12. **HotCRM at the unlock.** `src/sales/sharing/positions.ts` declares `permissionSets` on its positions (tagged `v6.0.0`), so its namesake sets arrive in `context.permissions` and are not probe candidates; its boot pin `test/demo-staffing.test.ts:485` (no fold event names a HotCRM position) keeps holding under the new predicate.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/24757-retire-position-name-fold.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`, `@objectstack/core` `patch`. Matches what the diff publishes: both packages move, no `@objectstack/spec` file changes, `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (no key, value, type or default an author writes moves), so `patch` is the level AGENTS.md assigns, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) present in the body. The banner carries Before / Now / Fix and the cloud ordering (HotCRM `v6.0.0` or later first). The repair round changes no published file and needs no changeset change.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: … ; widened: …)` on both the PR body and the changeset, read through `clause2-line.mjs`'s arm reader as value `yes`, arm `narrowing` (the arm word is the first token inside the parenthetical; the trailing colon is not an identifier character). **Right**: the diff narrows one surface (the plugin's effective grant set) and widens another (the two core types gain a field), which is exactly the `yes (narrowing)` case. The record's own face is the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the PR's paths also put it there through `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (governed). One precision for the maintainer: the core field is required, so "additive" is exact for readers of the types and a one-line migration (`directPermissions: []`) for out-of-repo code that constructs them; the changeset says so, and the previous head's own type-check red is the in-repo instance of that migration.
- The core change has no stored-artifact or authored-metadata source, so the ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition covers it as written.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Ruling A** (additive `directPermissions` on both core types; explain reads the dual case as `direct grant + position:P`; PR declares `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`): honoured, see ① items 5, 6 and ②.
- **Ruling S1** (self path re-resolves a human principal through `resolveUserAuthzGrants` and attaches only `directPermissions`; agent, guest and system unchanged): honoured, see ① item 7.
- **Previous head's `Type Check · workspace` red**: this PR's own (① item 6), repaired on this head by the migration the changeset prescribes; the dev's first-round typecheck reading covered core and plugin-security only and its "other packages passed" line read vitest, not tsc — the workspace lane is what caught it, and it is green here.
- **Dev flag: `PositionGrantVia` `'name'`, its docblock, the UI badge and `managedEnvironmentUsers.tsx` are #26022's** — answered: a published value nothing emits is an acceptable transitional state because no consumer grants on it; #26022 is open and blocked on this PR and should follow it.
- **Dev flag: stale prose naming the fold as live** — the core docblocks are corrected on this head (① item 11). What remains (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3376`, dogfood comments, fixture strings) is prose only, outside the claim's surface, with no behaviour on it; the rest docblock goes with #26022. Not a landing blocker.
